parents.description: When true, creates intermediate directories as needed (mkdir -p semantics).

mode.description: POSIX mode bits as a decimal integer; default 493 = 0o755. Ignored on Windows (NTFS uses ACLs, not POSIX modes).

created.description: True when the directory was newly created. Reserved for future semantics where `parents: true` may report which intermediate paths existed already.

x-implementations.name: create_directory_w
x-implementations.description: Win32 `CreateDirectoryW`. With `parents: true`, the agent walks the path components from the root, calling CreateDirectoryW for each missing component (existing intermediate dirs are skipped, not errored).

x-implementations.name: create_directory_a
x-implementations.description: Win32 `CreateDirectoryA` legacy fallback for NT 4 / 9x. ANSI path; transcoded UTF-8 → ANSI by the agent.

windows-modern.description: CreateDirectoryW. Long-path `\\?\` prefix automatic when input exceeds MAX_PATH. `parents: true` walks the path components, creating each missing one. ERR not_found when `parents: false` and a parent doesn't exist; ERR already_exists when the leaf already exists. The `mode` field is silently ignored — NTFS uses ACLs, not POSIX bits.

windows-classic.description: CreateDirectoryW on NT 5+; CreateDirectoryA on NT 4 / 9x. Same `parents: true` walking behaviour. No long-path support pre-NT-5.1 — paths over MAX_PATH return ERR not_found. The `mode` field is silently ignored.
